claims.explanation: ICI-162846 is annotated as an HRH2 (histamine H2 receptor) antagonist, but its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is not explained by HRH2 blockade alone; the strongest genomic correlate is enrichment of TP53 mutation and RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, NF1) among sensitive lines, with PIK3CA mutation and EGFR mutation enriched among resistant lines. This suggests the drug's selectivity may reflect a context-dependent interaction with p53-deficient, MAPK-driven tumors, possibly through off-target kinase or GPCR-linked signaling effects rather than canonical H2 antagonism. features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in nearly all strongly killed lines and is the most common alteration in the sensitive set
KRAS-mutant pancreatic, colorectal, ovarian and gastric lines are enriched among sensitive lines
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling and appears in multiple sensitive lines (BICR6, KALS1, S117, IPC298)
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines K029AX and IPC298 are selectively killed
NRAS-mutant lines KU1919 and IPC298 are among the most sensitive
PIK3CA mutation is enriched in the least-affected lines (HGC27, KYSE510, SNUC5, SNU840, MKN1)
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines NCIH1650, HCC4006 and NCIH1437 are among the least affected
PTEN mutation appears in several resistant lines (ZR751, HEC265, FTC133, UACC62) and in some sensitive lines, weakening but not excluding a protective trend
annotated drug target; higher HRH2 expression could increase dependence on H2-receptor signaling, though direct evidence is limited
GNAS is downregulated in the virtual-cell response, suggesting Gs-coupled signaling contributes to sensitivity
CTNNB1 mutation appears in sensitive gastric line KE39 and resistant endometrial line HEC265, so evidence is mixed and weak
SF3B1 mutation is present in sensitive kidney UO31 and lung HCC95 lines, but the mechanistic link is unclear

raw.explanation: ICI-162846 is annotated as an HRH2 (histamine H2 receptor) antagonist, but its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is not explained by HRH2 blockade alone; the strongest genomic correlate is enrichment of TP53 mutation and RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, NF1) among sensitive lines, with PIK3CA mutation and EGFR mutation enriched among resistant lines. This suggests the drug's selectivity may reflect a context-dependent interaction with p53-deficient, MAPK-driven tumors, possibly through off-target kinase or GPCR-linked signaling effects rather than canonical H2 antagonism. The virtual-cell response showing GNAS downregulation and similarity to GSK3/thromboxane-receptor modulators supports a signaling-network mechanism rather than simple histamine-receptor dependence.
